title: United Airlines 2885
summary: A DC-8 cargo flight crashed during takeoff from Detroit after an unauthorized seat swap placed an insufficiently trained flight engineer at the controls. The aircraft pitched nose-up to an excessive attitude, causing engine surges, wing bank, and a stall at approximately 1000 feet altitude. Investigation revealed the horizontal stabilizer was set to 7.5 units nose-up trim, likely due to inadequate pre-takeoff checklist procedures during the confusion of the crew change.
probable_cause: An excessively high stabilizer trim setting of 7.5 units nose-up during takeoff. Contributing factors included an unauthorized flight engineer performing the takeoff, the flight engineer's inadequate training and previous failed proficiency checks, and the captain's failure to correct the situation or prevent the unauthorized seat swap.

title: Turkish Airlines flight 158
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 158 operating a Boeing 727 crashed near Ankara Esenboğa Airport on 16 January 1983 in severe winter weather. The aircraft landed approximately 50 meters short of the runway in driving snow and gusty winds, struck an obstacle, broke into three pieces, and caught fire. The crash killed 47 of the 67 occupants on board, with most fatal injuries occurring in the middle section of the aircraft that caught fire.
probable_cause: The aircraft landed short of the runway in driving snow and severe weather conditions, struck an obstacle, broke apart and caught fire.

title: 1983 Avensa Douglas DC-9 crash
summary: Avensa Flight 007, a Douglas DC-9-32 operating a domestic Venezuelan flight from Caracas to Barquisimeto, made an ILS approach through thick fog and landed hard 1,015 meters beyond the runway threshold. The landing gear collapsed on impact. The aircraft skidded off the runway and exploded in a post-impact fire. Of 45 passengers and 5 crew on board, 23 were killed and 10 were seriously injured. The investigation determined improper in-flight decisions and inadequate supervision as probable causes.
probable_cause: Improper in-flight decisions and inadequate supervision of the flight were ruled to be the probable causes.

title: Air Canada 797
summary: Air Canada Flight 797 was enroute from Dallas to Montreal when an in-flight fire developed in the rear lavatory at 18:48. The fire spread between the outer skin and inner decor panels, filling the aircraft with toxic smoke and burning through electrical cables that disabled most cockpit instrumentation. The captain exercised outstanding airmanship to divert the aircraft to Cincinnati for an emergency landing. However, 90 seconds after landing and opening the exit doors, fresh oxygen entering the cabin created a backdraft that engulfed the interior in flames, killing 23 passengers trapped in the fuselage.
probable_cause: A fire of undetermined origin in the rear lavatory. The NTSB noted the flight crew underestimated the fire's severity and the decision to land at Cincinnati was correct, but the post-landing flashover during evacuation proved unsurvivable for those unable to escape.

title: 1983 Chosonminhang Ilyushin Il-62 crash
summary: A CAAK Il-62M carrying 17 passengers and 6 crew was operating an international charter flight from Pyongyang, North Korea to Conakry, Guinea via Bamako, Mali with construction cargo and North Korean workers ahead of the 1984 Organization of African Unity summit. summary: Captain Terán had received only three weeks of simulator training and 30 hours of Boeing 737 flight time. title: Aeroflot 5463
summary: The Tu-134A collided with Dolan Mountain during descent to Almaty. Air traffic control gave an erroneous instruction to turn and the crew mistakenly chose an incorrect heading of 199 degrees instead of 140. Although ATC subsequently corrected the heading, it instructed the crew to descend to 600 m where the minimum safe altitude was 4620 m. The crew chose to descend anyway instead of climbing when they knew they were on a collision course.

title: Korean Air Lines 007 crash
summary: Korean Air Lines Flight 007, a Boeing 747 flying from New York to Seoul via Anchorage, drifted off its planned route owing to a navigational mistake by the crew and flew through Soviet airspace on 1 September 1983. Soviet Air Forces treated the unidentified aircraft as an intruding US spy plane and destroyed it with air-to-air missiles from a Sukhoi Su-15 interceptor after firing warning shots; it crashed into the sea near Moneron Island, killing all 246 passengers and 23 crew.

title: Air Illinois 710
summary: An Air Illinois HS 748 crashed near Pinckneyville, Illinois after takeoff from Springfield. The first officer mistakenly isolated the right generator instead of the left, degrading electrical power. The crew failed to properly manage the remaining electrical load, and when the battery depleted, the aircraft lost flight instruments and navigation radios. The crew descended to 2400 feet and crashed in a hilly pasture. All 10 occupants were killed.

title: Nigeria Airways 250
summary: A Fokker F28 Fellowship descending on VOR approach to Enugu Airport in below-minimum visibility began descent prematurely approximately 3 km from the runway threshold. title: Madrid Runway Disaster
summary: An Aviaco DC-9 taxiing for takeoff on runway 01 accidentally made a wrong turn in dense fog and entered the active runway, directly into the path of an Iberia Boeing 727 beginning its takeoff roll. The 727 crew attempted to rotate for liftoff but had not achieved flying speed. The aircraft's rear fuselage struck the DC-9. Poor visibility combined with inadequate airport signage and taxiway markings prevented the DC-9 crew from recognizing they had taxied onto the runway.

title: Aeroflot 601
summary: Aeroflot Flight 601, an Antonov An-24RV, crashed near Leshukonskoye on 24 December 1983 while attempting to land. The captain descended with a significant left deviation of about 490 meters and decided to land instead of executing a go-around, then banked right to correct. At 30 meters altitude he attempted a go-around but the aircraft reached critical slip angles and stalled. After reaching 90 degrees left bank angle at 80 meters altitude, the aircraft crashed 110 meters right of the runway. Forty-four of 49 occupants were killed.
probable_cause: The investigation placed responsibility on Captain Alimov, who displayed risky piloting style that violated flight instructions. The crew should have initiated a go-around instead of attempting to land first, and the premature go-around attempt at low altitude resulted in a stall and loss of control.
